source.document: FD&C Act section 502, 21 U.S.C. 352 (Misbranded drugs and devices)

rules.rule_text: A drug is misbranded if its labeling (incl. promotional labeling) is false or misleading in any particular. Umbrella rule; Margin routes to the specific rules below.
rules.verbatim_quote: If its labeling is false or misleading in any particular.
rules.applies_to: all promotional labeling (HCP, DTC, payer, social, exhibit, email)

detection.question: Taken as a whole, does the piece create a false or misleading net impression about the drug in any particular?
detection.pass_anchor: Every express and implied claim is consistent with the PI and supported; net impression matches the label.
detection.fail_anchor: Any express or implied claim (text, visual, audio) would leave a reasonable reader with an impression the PI/data do not support.

source.document: FD&C Act section 502, 21 U.S.C. 352 (Misbranded drugs and devices)

rules.rule_text: Every Rx drug advertisement must include the established name (prominently, in type at least half as large as the proprietary name) and a true statement in brief summary of side effects, contraindications and effectiveness.
rules.verbatim_quote: the established name ... printed prominently and in type at least half as large as that used for any trade or brand name thereof
rules.applies_to: advertisements (DTC, HCP journal, broadcast, digital ads)

detection.logic: For every proprietary-name occurrence that is featured (headline/first mention per page/web page/SUPER), the established name must occur within 60 characters (after stripping ®/™/CII); when font metadata is supplied, established-name size >= 0.5x brand size.

source.document: FD&C Act section 502, 21 U.S.C. 352 (Misbranded drugs and devices)

rules.rule_text: Published DTC ads must carry the statutory MedWatch statement.
rules.verbatim_quote: You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch, or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

detection.logic: If audience==DTC and piece_type is published/print ad: require 'fda.gov/medwatch' AND '1-800-FDA-1088' (dash/space tolerant).

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Broadcast ads must contain a brief summary or make adequate provision for dissemination of the approved labeling (toll-free number, website, print-ad reference, HCP referral).
rules.verbatim_quote: unless adequate provision is made for dissemination of the approved or permitted product labeling in connection with the broadcast presentation

detection.logic: For broadcast pieces: require >=3 of 4 adequate-provision elements: phone number pattern; URL; reference to a print ad/magazine; 'ask your doctor/pharmacist/health care provider'. Fail lists the missing elements.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Broadcast ads must state the major side effects and contraindications ('major statement') in the audio (or audio and visual) portion.
rules.verbatim_quote: Include information relating to the major side effects and contraindications ("major statement") of the advertised drugs in the audio or audio and visual parts of the presentation

detection.logic: Given pi.required_risk_terms (Boxed Warning concepts, all contraindications, W&P headings / MG 'most important information' items), each term (or listed synonym) must appear in the audio transcript (falls back to full text if no transcript). Fail lists missing terms.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Reminder ads (exempt from brief summary) may call attention to the drug name but may not include indications or dosage recommendations; a piece that names the product and its use is not a reminder ad.
rules.verbatim_quote: Reminder advertisements are those which call attention to the name of the drug product but do not include indications or dosage recommendations for use of the drug product.

detection.logic: If meta.claimed_reminder or no risk content: fail when the brand co-occurs with any indication/disease term (pi.indication_terms or a disease lexicon) or dosing language.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: An ad is not a 'true statement' if it is false or misleading with respect to side effects, contraindications, or effectiveness (covers overstatement of efficacy).
rules.verbatim_quote: It is false or misleading with respect to side effects, contraindications, or effectiveness

detection.question: Does the piece represent or suggest efficacy (magnitude, onset, durability, proportion of responders, outcomes) beyond what the PI/pivotal data show?
detection.pass_anchor: Efficacy statements match PI endpoints, magnitudes, timepoints and responder proportions, with the comparator shown.
detection.fail_anchor: Implies more patients, bigger, faster, longer-lasting, or different benefits than the PI supports (e.g., 'clear skin that lasts' when <50% achieve it).

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Fair balance: risk information must be presented with comparable depth/detail to effectiveness information.
rules.verbatim_quote: It fails to present a fair balance between information relating to side effects and contraindications and information relating to effectiveness of the drug

detection.logic: If the piece makes a benefit/indication claim (brand + benefit or indication lexicon), it must also contain risk content: an ISI header or >=2 risk markers (warning, contraindicated, side effect(s), serious, risk of, may cause, allergic). Excerpt-level check; complemented by A-202-E7-08 judgment for prominence.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Ads must reveal facts material in light of their representations or with respect to consequences of use (omission of material risk or indication facts).
rules.verbatim_quote: It fails to reveal facts material in the light of its representations or material with respect to consequences that may result from the use of the drug

detection.logic: Each pi.required_risk_terms item (boxed warning concepts, contraindications, W&P headings with their key action/severity words) must appear in the piece. Fail lists missing items.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Lexical trigger for efficacy overstatement: absolute, cure/heal, speed/onset, durability and totality words in efficacy claims must be verified against PI endpoints (fail-pending-verification).
rules.verbatim_quote: It is false or misleading with respect to side effects, contraindications, or effectiveness

detection.logic: Flag cure|cures|eliminat\w*|heal(s|ing)?|100 ?%|100 percent|complete(ly)? (relief|response|clear)|clear skin|lasting|lasts|durable|fast|rapid(ly)?|quick(ly)?|works (with)?in \d+|in (about )?\d+[-–]?\d* minutes|as soon as|live longer|treat all|doesn'?t come back|vaccine|guarantee\w*|proven|99 ?%|\d+(\.\d+)?\s*(x|times) more. Passes only if meta.substantiated_claims contains the matched span.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Exclusivity/priority claims ('only', 'first and only', '#1', 'leading', 'preferred') must be verified against approved products and labeling.

detection.logic: Flag (the )?(first and )?only|first[- ]in[- ]class|#1|number one|leading|preferred (choice|treatment)|another (topical )?(treatment )?option ... approved; pass if meta.substantiated_claims contains the span.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Ad must not represent or suggest the drug is useful in a broader range of conditions or patients than the labeling supports.
rules.verbatim_quote: useful in a broader range of conditions or patients ... than has been demonstrated by substantial evidence

detection.logic: Given pi.indication_qualifiers (population e.g. 'adults', line of therapy, 'in combination with X', 'adjunct to diet', 'acute', limitations of use), every qualifier must appear (case-insensitive, synonym list) in the piece where the indication/use is first stated. Fail lists missing qualifiers.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Judgment counterpart for broadening: implied use beyond indication (umbrella disease terms, 'all cancers', prevention vs treatment).
rules.verbatim_quote: useful in a broader range of conditions or patients

detection.question: Does the piece, through words or visuals, suggest use in a population, disease scope, line of therapy or regimen broader than the PI indication?
detection.pass_anchor: Indication stated with all PI qualifiers; visuals/patient types consistent with the indicated population.
detection.fail_anchor: Umbrella terms, imagery or phrasing implying broader populations, disease subsets or monotherapy beyond the label.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: No comparative claim that a drug is safer or more effective than another unless demonstrated by substantial evidence (generally adequate head-to-head trials).
rules.verbatim_quote: Contains a drug comparison that represents or suggests that a drug is safer or more effective than another drug in some particular when it has not been demonstrated

detection.logic: Trigger (fail-pending-substantiation) on comparative/superiority language: better|superior|more effective|outperform|vs\.?|versus|compared (to|with)|than [A-Z]|unlike other|preferred (choice|treatment)|x times|N% more. Passes only if meta.substantiated_claims lists the matched span (head-to-head support on file).

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: No representation that a drug is safer than demonstrated (minimization: 'well tolerated', 'no X side effects', 'hype', 'very rare', causality-disclaiming language).
rules.verbatim_quote: Contains a representation or suggestion that a drug is safer than it has been demonstrated to be

detection.logic: Flag: safe(r|st)? (as a claim, not 'safety information'), well[- ]tolerated, no (overall )?[a-z ,-]*(side effects|risk|liver injury)|minimal (effect|impact|risk), (over)?hyp(e|ed), very rare, mild to moderate, medicines have side effects, whether drug related or not, gentle, non-?toxic.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Judgment counterpart: minimization through framing, ordering, tone or selective presentation.
rules.verbatim_quote: safer than it has been demonstrated to be by substantial evidence or substantial clinical experience

detection.question: Does the piece downplay the seriousness, frequency or relevance of any labeled risk (framing, order, tone, selective data)?
detection.pass_anchor: Risks stated plainly with severity/action words from the PI; order follows label hierarchy; no softening language.
detection.fail_anchor: Risks framed as rare, mild, overhyped or generic; serious risks buried after minor ones; causality disclaimed.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: No nonclinical (animal/in vitro) data presented to suggest clinical significance not established.
rules.verbatim_quote: Contains favorable data or conclusions from nonclinical studies of a drug, such as in laboratory animals or in vitro, in a way that suggests they have clinical significance

detection.logic: Flag in vitro|in vivo|preclinical|animal (model|stud)|murine|mice|rats?|cell line|nonclinical unless the same sentence carries a 'clinical significance (has not been|unknown)' disclaimer.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: References/guidelines must actually support the claim (e.g., guideline category and preference claims must match the current guideline).
rules.verbatim_quote: Uses literature, quotations, or references that purport to support an advertising claim but in fact do not support the claim

detection.logic: Trigger on NCCN|ASCO|ESMO|guideline(s)|category [12][AB]?|preferred (regimen|recommendation|option): pass only if meta.reference_checks confirms the cited version and wording.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: No misleading statement that a drug differs from or does not contain a named drug or category of drugs.
rules.verbatim_quote: Uses statements or representations that a drug differs from or does not contain a named drug or category of drugs ... in a way that suggests falsely or misleadingly

detection.logic: Flag '(is )?not an? <class>' / 'unlike other <class>' / 'non-<class>' / 'no <class>' patterns (class lexicon: antipsychotic, opioid, steroid, stimulant, chemo(therapy), hormone, benzodiazepine, NSAID, immunosuppressant) for verification against PI section 12.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Headlines, subheadlines and graphics must not be misleading on their own.
rules.verbatim_quote: Uses headline, subheadline, or pictorial or other graphic matter in a way that is misleading

detection.question: Read alone, does any headline, tagline, graphic or image convey a claim the body/PI does not support?
detection.pass_anchor: Headline claims are fully qualified on their face or are non-claims.
detection.fail_anchor: A headline or visual carries an unqualified efficacy/safety/population message (e.g., 'CLEAR SKIN that lasts', imagery of off-label patient).

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Favorable conclusions from studies inadequate in design to support them (e.g., time-to-event / DCR / stable disease from single-arm trials) are misleading.
rules.verbatim_quote: Contains favorable information or conclusions from a study that is inadequate in design, scope, or conduct to furnish significant support

detection.logic: If pi.trial_design == 'single-arm' (or text says single-arm/open-label/non-randomized): flag PFS|OS|overall survival|progression-free|median (PFS|OS|survival)|time to|event-free|cystectomy-free|disease-specific survival|DCR|disease control|stable disease|SD|waterfall|tumor (change|shrinkage) . Disclaimers do not clear the flag.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Do not use statistical significance (p-values) to support claims lacking clinical significance or from non-prespecified analyses.
rules.verbatim_quote: Uses the concept of "statistical significance" to support a claim that has not been demonstrated to have clinical significance or validity

detection.logic: Flag p-values (p\s*[<=≤]\s*0?\.\d+) or 'statistically significant' when the piece or meta labels the endpoint exploratory/descriptive/secondary-not-controlled.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Retrospective/post hoc/exploratory analyses may not be presented as if confirmatory.
rules.verbatim_quote: Uses statistical analyses and techniques on a retrospective basis to discover and cite findings not soundly supported by the study

detection.logic: Flag post[- ]hoc|exploratory|subgroup|sub-?analysis|descriptive analysis|separate analysis|pooled analysis|open-label extension|not (prespecified|powered|controlled for multiplicity) when in the same piece as proven|demonstrated|showed|significant|%|x more. Also flags onset claims ('as soon as N hours/weeks') when meta.endpoint_status marks the timepoint exploratory.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Risk information must have prominence and readability reasonably comparable to effectiveness information (type size, placement, contrast, timing, narration).
rules.verbatim_quote: Fails to present information relating to side effects and contraindications with a prominence and readability reasonably comparable with the presentation of information relating to effectiveness

detection.question: Is the risk information presented with prominence and readability reasonably comparable to the benefit claims (size, contrast, placement, timing, narration, white space)?
detection.pass_anchor: Risk is as noticeable and readable as benefit: same modality, similar size/contrast, not buried after sign-off or in collapsed/scrolling windows.
detection.fail_anchor: Risk is smaller, faster, text-only while benefits are narrated, placed after the close/sign-off, collapsed, or crowded.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Deterministic proxy for risk placement in time-ordered media: risk content must not first appear only after a closing cue.
rules.verbatim_quote: with a prominence and readability reasonably comparable

detection.logic: With ordered segments (meta.segments or text order): find first closing cue (visit|learn more at|brought to you by|see you|sign-off/signature|tag line|end card). Fail if all risk markers occur after it.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Deterministic proxy for comparable prominence in audiovisual media: if benefits are narrated, risk must be narrated; risk airtime should not be a small fraction of benefit airtime.
rules.applies_to: TV, online video, social video, podcasts

detection.logic: Requires meta.timing {benefit_narrated, risk_narrated, benefit_seconds, risk_seconds}: fail if benefit narrated and risk not, or risk_seconds < 0.25 x benefit_seconds (Margin heuristic).

source.document: 21 CFR 201.57 Specific requirements on content and format of labeling (PLR)

rules.rule_text: Indications are defined by the PI, including major limitations of use; promotional indication statements should carry the population and limitation-of-use qualifiers.
rules.verbatim_quote: Major limitations of use (e.g., lack of effect in particular subsets of the population, or second line therapy status) must be briefly noted.

detection.logic: Same check as A-202-E6-01, with pi.limitations_of_use terms appended to required qualifiers.

source.document: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(3)(i) (Form FDA 2253 at time of initial dissemination) - section as cited in the OPDP letters; regulation text not fetched in this pass

rules.rule_text: Promotional labeling and ads must be submitted to FDA on Form FDA 2253 at the time of initial dissemination/publication.
rules.applies_to: all disseminated promotional pieces incl. executive/media appearances, paid search, social

detection.logic: Metadata: if meta.disseminated is true (or first_use_date set) and meta.form_2253_id is empty -> fail. Pre-dissemination: warn.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Ads may recommend or suggest only uses in the approved labeling; investigational products/uses may not be promoted as safe or effective.
rules.verbatim_quote: may recommend and suggest the drug only for those uses contained in the labeling thereof

detection.logic: If meta.investigational (or text names a development code like ABC-1234 with no approval): require 'investigational' AND ('not approved' or 'safety and efficacy (have not been|not) established'); fail on efficacy/safety claims (proven|safe|effective|no side effects) about it.

source.document: 21 CFR 202.1 Prescription-drug advertisements (eCFR current; read via LII)

rules.rule_text: Judgment counterpart: off-label suggestion (disease, population, route) not in the PI.
rules.verbatim_quote: only for those uses contained in the labeling

detection.question: Does the piece suggest any use, population, regimen or route not in the PI indication?
detection.pass_anchor: All suggested uses are within the PI; unapproved uses are absent or confined to compliant SIUU/payer channels with disclosures.
detection.fail_anchor: Any suggestion of an unapproved use (e.g., 'can treat all cancers').
